clue.text: Floater second in this seconds behind first to show?

definitions.text: Floater second in this seconds behind first to show?

indicators.note: 'second in' asks for the letter standing in position two of the word that follows
'first to' asks only for the opening letter of the word that comes after it

blocks.note: a floater is crude slang for a lump of excrement that will not flush
the second letter of this
the opening letter of show
ticks are moments, informally seconds; 'behind' places them after the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which floating stick came second in a race, just seconds behind the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: in POOHSTICKS, the game from Winnie-the-Pooh, players drop sticks off a bridge and see whose floats out first.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's game each player's stick is a floater racing downstream, and coming second means emerging seconds after the winner.

clue.text: I'm done talking balls

definitions.note: plural noun phrase for a single set of deliveries

blocks.note: first meaning: the radio word that ends a turn to speak
second meaning: in cricket, a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' looks like an exclamation of disgust tacked on to a speech; it is cricket. A cricket over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio users say it to hand the channel back, and cricket's unit of six deliveries carries the same name.

clue.text: Sackcloth smeared in ashes

indicators.note: something smeared is messed up and spread about, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A penitent in sackcloth and ashes, the biblical image of mourning and repentance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse jute fabric used for sacks, so it is literally a sacking cloth.

clue.text: Bird regularly sat near strange stinky flower

indicators.note: 'regularly' means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
the second, fourth and sixth letters of these two words
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A bird perched beside a peculiar flower that smells awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like an anagram signal, but here it simply supplies its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The titan arum is a giant tropical bloom nicknamed the corpse flower for its rotting-meat smell.

clue.text: One arranging actor's credit in lead for Gladiator?

definitions.text: One arranging actor's credit in lead for Gladiator?

indicators.note: arranging means putting things into a new order, so the following letters are reordered
the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, possessive S included
the opening letter of Gladiator

explanation.surface: Someone sorting out the billing for whoever plays the lead in the film Gladiator.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: picking the star of Gladiator is exactly what this person does.
explanation.definitionFit: This film professional chooses performers for roles, so they would be the one finding a lead actor for a movie.

clue.text: Insertion of long key?

blocks.note: surface reading: fitting an extended key into a lock
setter's reading: what you put into text by pressing the widest bar on a keyboard

explanation.walkthrough: The keyboard's longest key is the one between words; pressing it inserts a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the long bar at the bottom of a keyboard inserts a blank gap between words in typed text.

clue.text: More or less potty don

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, meaning approximately
a po is a chamber pot, a child's potty

explanation.surface: A university lecturer described as somewhat crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like an adjective meaning daft and 'don' like an Oxbridge academic; both mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Mafia a capo is a boss heading a crime family or crew, the same figure called a don.

clue.text: Trick to keep lips red

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a con is a swindle or trick
lips are the edges of a cup or bowl, its rims

explanation.surface: Using a trick to keep one's lips looking red, like long-lasting lipstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of the colour, so it serves as a synonym for this hue.

clue.text: Bars over entrance left copper climbing window ledge

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the ledge below a window

explanation.surface: A thief left copper by climbing in over a window ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy grating lowered over a castle gateway, a grid of bars guarding the way in.

clue.text: Leisure time after priest's last afternoon service

indicators.note: 'last' asks only for the final letter of the word before it
'after' sends the leisure and time pieces second, behind the priest's letter

blocks.note: the final letter of priest
ease is relaxation or leisure
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A priest enjoys some leisure time once his afternoon church service is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts EASE and T after the priest's last letter. 'Service' feels like a church service but is a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A service is a matching set of crockery, and the one for afternoon tea has cups, saucers and a pot.

clue.text: European put waste pipe back on bath

indicators.note: putting something back means facing it the other way, so its letters run in reverse

blocks.note: a spa is a bath or resort with healing waters, like the city of Bath
a drain carries away waste water

explanation.surface: A plumber fitting a waste pipe to the back of a bathtub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the reversed pipe after SPA in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Spain is a European, so the general term stands in for the specific nationality.

clue.text: Designer's private commemorative event curtailed twice by church

indicators.note: curtailing removes a tail, and doing it twice drops the final two letters

blocks.note: a GI is an American private soldier
a yearly date marking a past event
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's private memorial event, cut short twice by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' puts CE alongside the shortened word. The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni Versace was the Italian fashion designer who founded the luxury label bearing his surname.

clue.text: French lady worried air is cracking pasta

indicators.note: worried means agitated or disturbed, so the letters are jumbled
cracking something means breaking into it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the letters rearranged
penne is tube-shaped pasta

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman fretting that air bubbles are cracking her pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parisienne is a woman from Paris, a specific kind of Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Mother wearing a dress rather than trousers for the high street

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother

blocks.clueFragment: wearing a dress rather than trousers
blocks.note: a man in drag wears women's clothes such as a dress

explanation.surface: Mum chose a dress over trousers for her trip to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says Mother herself wears the dress, which needs no drag; the cryptic reading clothes a man in women's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The main drag is American slang for a town's principal thoroughfare, what Britons call the high street.

clue.text: Squeeze water out of a thousand fish

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Wringing water out of a catch of a thousand fish.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this means to press wet laundry between rollers, wringing the moisture from it.

clue.text: Police force enjoyed taking Ecstasy, as change from heroin

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
had in the sense of enjoyed or experienced
someone taking a drug is on it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Police officers took ecstasy for a change instead of heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Methadone is a synthetic opioid prescribed as a substitute for addicts coming off heroin.

clue.text: Limited by shortfall, is someone able to change supply?

definitions.note: adjectival phrase; supply is the adverb from supple

indicators.note: letters limited by these words are bounded within them, sitting inside the run of text

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of shortfall, all of is, and the start of someone

explanation.surface: A business question: can someone, limited by a shortfall, change the supply of goods?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as the noun about goods but is the adverb of supple, pronounced supp-lee.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom means lithe and flexible, so a lissom body can shift position in a supple, bending way.

clue.text: Like that duck, prepare to lay eggs without delay

blocks.note: so means in that way
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like the letter O
birds nest before laying

explanation.surface: Like that duck over there, get ready to lay eggs right away.
explanation.definitionFit: Soonest means at the earliest possible moment, as in 'the sooner the better', so it is immediate.

clue.text: Part of song currently going around

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: an air is a tune, so a component of one sits within that tune
second meaning: talked about or felt everywhere at the moment, like a rumour

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: a song is an air, so any part of it is literally inside the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour or mood that is widely sensed right now is said to be floating about everywhere, circulating.

clue.text: Randy Conservative got out of trousers

indicators.note: trousers is read as a verb, to pocket, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: exited means left or got out
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A lustful Tory politician caught with his trousers off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like the garment in a political sex scandal; it is the verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for sexually aroused, a sense of the participle used for stirred up.

clue.text: Fix sticker on chic patient undergoing treatment

indicators.note: something undergoing treatment is being worked on and altered, so the letters change order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse fixes a sticker on a stylish patient receiving treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a verb telling you to attach the sticker; it is a noun, a smoker's dose.
explanation.definitionFit: This adhesive patch on the skin delivers a smoker's craving dose, or fix, of the drug, so it is a sticker giving a fix.

clue.text: Italian trains turned up, going nowhere

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means flipped to read bottom to top

blocks.note: treni is the Italian word for trains

explanation.surface: Italian trains finally arrived but went nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as arrived, a joke at the railway's expense; in a down entry it means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert describes something motionless and lacking the power to move, so it stays put.

clue.text: Son landed upside down in fall on slopes?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A skiing son landed on his head during a tumble on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' reads as a tumble on the piste; it is precipitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers rely on precipitation of frozen flakes, so a fall of it on mountain pistes is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Find there's no head on English coin, shocking

indicators.note: with no head, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its front
E is the abbreviation for English
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A collector finds an English coin with no monarch's head on it and is shocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means offensive to accepted standards of propriety, which is what outrageous behaviour does.

clue.text: Jolly dictator beheaded in self-inflicted blunder

indicators.note: beheading removes the top, so the word loses its first letter
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: Vladimir Putin, Russia's autocratic leader
OG is an own goal, a football blunder scored against your own side

explanation.surface: A dictator's execution turns out to be an own goal for his regime.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a jolly is a pleasure trip or jaunt, often at someone else's expense, so a day out.

clue.text: Live theatre something you're partial to?

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: Live theatre is something you are fond of.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination or liking, a particular leaning toward some activity.

clue.text: Unruly youth unhappy given vase to hold refused

indicators.note: being given something to hold means wrapping around it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rebellious 1950s British youth
an urn is a large vase
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A miserable delinquent is handed a vase and declines to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be declined is the sense of this phrasal verb, as when an offer or application gets rejected.
